# LMDB facade fixture corpus.
#
# One record per line: key, a single TAB, value. A '#' starts a comment and
# blank lines are ignored. Every byte is printable ASCII other than the TAB
# separator, and no byte is a backslash, so this file can be compared directly
# against the body of an `mdb_dump -p` of the environment it produced.
#
# The two blocks below are deliberate and different:
#
#   [insert] is the order the writer stores the records in.
#   [expect] is the order a forward cursor must hand them back in, written
#            down here rather than computed, so the test compares the C's
#            collation against an answer recorded by hand.
#
# The default collation is memcmp over the common prefix with the shorter item
# first (mdb.c:6659-6675), so the expected order is `Zulu` (0x5A) before the
# lowercase keys, `alpha` before `alphabet` because it is a prefix of it, and
# `delta` before `gamma`.
#
# `delta` has an empty value, which is what makes the reader's zero-length
# case observable: a key must be at least one byte, a value need not be.

[insert]
gamma	third
alpha	first
Zulu	fourth
alphabet	sixth
beta	second
delta	

[expect]
Zulu	fourth
alpha	first
alphabet	sixth
beta	second
delta	
gamma	third
